newsitem.title: USA: Healthsouth buys ReadiCare for $70 million.
newsitem.headline: Healthsouth buys ReadiCare for $70 million.

text.p: Healthsouth Corp. said Wednesday it signed a definitive agreement to buy ReadiCare Inc., a provider of occupational healthcare services and related cost-containment programmes, for about $70 million.
The deal, approved by both companies' boards, calls for Healthsouth to offer 0.2425 share of its stock for each ReadCare share in a tax-free pooling of interests.
The exchange ratio would be adjusted if Healthsouth's average stock price rises above $38.30 per share or falls below $30.60 over a certain period.
Sunnyvale, Calif.-based ReadiCare rose $2.625 to $7.75 on Nasdaq, while Healthsouth's stock fell 62.5 cents to $34.625 on the New York Stock Exchange at midday.

"This transaction will complement our existing facilities in California and Washington, and our lines of business are a natural fit," said Richard M. Scrushy, chairman and chief executive officer of Birmingham, Ala.-based Healthsouth.
Healthsouth provides outpatient surgery and rehabilitative healthcare services through more than 1,000 locations nationwide. ReadiCare has 37 sites in California and Washington.
The deal is expected to close in the fourth quarter, subject to approval by ReadiCare stockholders and regulators.
Healthsouth said it has received proxies for the deal from ReadiCare's senior managers and directors, who together own about 9.5 percent of ReadiCare's stock.
ReadiCare has to pay an $8 million break-up fee if the transaction is ended under certain conditions.
